chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Fadl, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when the people did what they did by pledging allegiance to Abu Bakr, nothing prevented the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) from calling the people to himself, except that he looked at the people and feared for them that they would revert from Islam, so they would worship idols and not testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And it was more beloved to him that he should confirm them upon what they had done rather than them reverting from all of Islam.

And indeed, those who undertook what they undertook what they undertook are the ones who perished. But as for the one who did not do that, and entered into what the people entered into without knowledge and without enmity towards the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), then that does not make him a disbeliever, nor does it take him out of Islam.
And for this reason, Ali (peace be upon him) concealed his matter, and pledged allegiance unwillingly, since he did not find helpers.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) not immediately claim the caliphate after the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the strategic patience (hilm) of Imam Ali (AS), who prioritized the preservation of the core tenet of Tawhid over immediate political assertion, fearing that a power struggle would lead to total apostasy (Riddah). It establishes a key Shia theological principle distinguishing between those who pledged allegiance out of ignorance or political expediency versus those who actively opposed the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby preserving the faith of the majority. This context underscores the concept of 'Taqiyya' and the pragmatic concealment of Imamate rights until sufficient support was available.

en.hubeali: H 14902 – Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad Al-Kindy, from someone else, from Abaan Bin Usmaan, from Al-Fazel, from Zurara, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’far asws has said that:

‘The people, when they did what they did, they pledged their allegiances to Abu Bakr, nothing prevented Amir-ul- Momineen<sup>asws</sup> calling the people to himself<sup>asws</sup> except that he<sup>asws</sup> looked around at the people and feared for them that they would renege from Al-Islam, and resort to worshipping the idols and not testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and that Muhamamd<sup>saww</sup> is the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and it was more beloved to him<sup>asws</sup> than he<sup>asws</sup> should agree with them upon what they had done rather than them reneging against the whole of Al-Islam.

But rather, destroyed is the one who does what they did. So, as for the one who did not do that, and entered into what the people had entered into without knowledge or enmity against Amir-ul- Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, so for that they have neither blasphemed nor exited from Al-Islam,
and it is for that reason that Ali<sup>asws</sup> concealed his<sup>asws</sup> matter, and had to pledge allegiance unwillingly, when he<sup>asws</sup> did not find any helpers’.
en.sarwar: 455. Narrated to us Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ali Bin Al-No’man, from Abdullah Bin Muskaan, from Abdul Raheem Al-Qaseer who said:

I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s.) that the people are appalled when we say that the people turned apostate’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘O Abdul Raheem, after the passing away of the Rasool Allah (saww), the people turned to the terms of ignorance. The Helpers were isolated and their isolation was not in goodness. They went and pledged their allegiances to Sa’d and were shouting slogans of the era of ignorance, ‘O Sa’d, you are the hope, and you are the vessel, and the solution!’
